E-001.threat: JTAG privilege escalation — attacker gains full processor control via JTAG interface
E-001.cause: JTAG interface is accessible and not locked via OTP fuse
E-001.attack: Attacker connects JTAG probe, halts CPU, reads/writes memory and bypasses all software security controls

E-002.threat: Secure Boot disable via RDP downgrade — attacker removes all debug protection
E-002.cause: RDP Level 2 not applied — JTAG can be re-enabled allowing firmware modification
E-002.attack: Attacker uses unlocked JTAG to disable Secure Boot verification and install persistent malicious firmware

E-003.threat: Embedded process privilege escalation — attacker gains elevated access on embedded process
E-003.cause: Debug interface or privileged API accessible without proper authentication
E-003.attack: Attacker exploits embedded process debug interface to execute code with elevated privileges

E-004.threat: Embedded system privilege escalation — attacker gains elevated access on embedded controller
E-004.cause: Debug interfaces or privileged commands accessible without authentication
E-004.attack: Attacker exploits debug interface to execute code with system-level authority on the embedded controller

E-005.threat: Secure boot bypass on embedded system — attacker bypasses firmware signature verification
E-005.cause: Secure Boot is not enforced or can be bypassed via debug interface
E-005.attack: Attacker disables Secure Boot to execute malicious firmware that persists across device resets
